findings.title: Filing a bug report passes authorization with no credential: hunter attribution rests on an unauthenticated form field
findings.note: POST /api/v1/bounty/reports with an empty body returns a byte-identical validation error with no key and with a TRUSTED key. No authorization check runs before validation. If that holds for a populated body, hunter_name is a field any caller sets freely and reward attribution is unauthenticated. SCOPE: an empty body shows only that auth does not run FIRST. It does not show a fully-populated anonymous POST is accepted -- testing that would create a real record in their tracker, so it is asked, not done. Verified after probing that the tracker total was unchanged at 23.

findings.title: Does llms.txt quote the same agent count in all of its own sentences?
findings.note: A document that contradicts itself is worse than two documents that disagree, because the reader has no way to pick. Added after report #52 updated one occurrence of the count and left another behind.

findings.title: Does every tool name llms.txt documents exist on the server?
findings.note: Subset, not set_equal. llms.txt is not obliged to list every tool -- it is obliged not to name one that does not exist. The earlier set_equal form would now fail simply because the document lists fewer than the server serves, which is correct behaviour.

findings.title: 11 reports filed under our hunter name were closed by the platform and have never been re-verified by us
findings.note: The resolution notes are specific -- they name files, line numbers and commit hashes. That is better than most vendors provide and it is worth crediting. It is still a claim: the commits are not inspectable from here, validated_at is null, and our own records still list these as open with last_regression_run: null. Correct state is FIX_CLAIMED, not fixed. Note also that all six are UI defects in arena.js, outside this project's API/MCP scope -- re-verifying them needs the browser suite, not this one.

findings.title: Is agent-skills.json the actionable subset of agent-card.json, as stated?

detail.agent_card: {ai-due-diligence, ai-native-provenance, arena-trading, clone-ai-agent, et10-revenue-share, exchange-tokens, live-headlines, market-data, prop-desk-trading, smart-delegation, tge-prediction-markets, trade-event-cards ... (+1 more)}  n=13
detail.agent_skills: {arena-trading, asset-discovery, clone-ai-agent, et10-revenue-share, exchange-tokens, market-data, portfolio-management, prop-desk-trading, trade-event-cards, trade-prediction-markets}  n=10

findings.note: Their resolution on #51 states agent-card.json is the full discovery card and agent-skills.json the endpoint-actionable subset. That is a testable model and the right one, so this checks the claim they actually made rather than demanding the two files be identical -- which they explained, correctly, that they should not be.

findings.title: 10 documented URLs exist but reject the documented method
findings.note: llms.txt renders MCP tools as fetchable URLs of the form /mcp/v1/tools/<name>. They answer 405: the resource exists, the shape in the document does not. Low severity on its own, but it is the same document that carries the tool names and counts.
